```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
#                      DEEPOL Biogeography - Full Setup Chunk
# ==============================================================================
#
# Loads all required packages, sets up directory structure, color and shape 
# palettes, key configuration parameters, and core helper functions for the 
# entire notebook. This ensures full reproducibility and clarity.
# ==============================================================================

# ---- Load libraries ----------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)    # Core data wrangling and visualization (dplyr, ggplot2, etc.)
  library(tibble)       # Enhanced data frames
  library(ggplot2)      # Explicit ggplot2 load (redundant if tidyverse, but good for clarity)
  library(vegan)        # Multivariate stats & diversity (ordination, PERMANOVA)
  library(here)         # File path handling (project-rooted, cross-platform)
  library(patchwork)    # Advanced plot layout/composition
  library(conflicted)   # Handling function conflicts (e.g. filter, select)
  library(ggforce)      # Extra geoms for ggplot2
  library(reshape2)     # Legacy data reshaping (melt, dcast, etc.)
  library(ape)          # Phylogenetics tools
  library(ggtree)       # Phylogenetic tree visualization and annotation
  library(grid)         # Fine-tuned plot arrangement
  library(ggnewscale)   # Multiple fill/color scales on one ggplot
  library(maps)         # World map polygons
  library(UpSetR)       # UpSet plots for set intersections
  library(purrr)        # Functional programming tools (map, reduce, etc.)
  library(sf)           # Spatial features (distance to coast)
  library(rnaturalearth) # Natural Earth coastline (also needs 'rnaturalearthdata' installed)
  library(broom)        # Tidy model output (glm/lm coefficients)
})

# ---- Resolve dplyr conflicts to avoid ambiguity ------------------------------
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::lag)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select)

# ---- Output directory structure ----------------------------------------------
# Root for all figures/tables
output_root <- here("results")
if (!dir.exists(output_root)) dir.create(output_root, recursive = TRUE)
# Define main lineage codes
lineages <- c("DEEPOL1", "DEEPOL2", "DEEPOL3")
# Create and register per-lineage subfolders for outputs
output_dirs <- setNames(
  vapply(lineages, function(lin) {
    dir <- file.path(output_root, lin)
    if (!dir.exists(dir)) dir.create(dir, recursive = TRUE)
    dir
  }, character(1)),
  lineages
)
# Use: file.path(output_dirs["DEEPOL1"], "filename.pdf")

# ---- Color and shape palettes for figures -----------------------------------
# Colors for each main lineage
lineage_colours <- c(
  DEEPOL1 = "cornflowerblue",
  DEEPOL2 = "mediumpurple3",
  DEEPOL3 = "mediumseagreen"
)
# Custom colors by named ocean for mapping
ocean_colours <- c(
  "Arctic Ocean"         = "deepskyblue2",
  "Southern Ocean"       = "slateblue2",
  "North Atlantic Ocean" = "seagreen",
  "South Atlantic Ocean" = "yellowgreen",
  "North Pacific Ocean"  = "orange2",
  "South Pacific Ocean"  = "gold2",
  "Indian Ocean"         = "orchid2",
  "Mediterranean Region" = "coral"
)
# Point shape by ocean layer
layer_shapes <- c("sunlit" = 16, "dark" = 17)
# Pre-set ellipse fill palettes for plot facets
ellipse_fill_palettes <- list(
  polar_group = c("polar" = "slateblue2", "non-polar" = "coral"),
  ocean_layer = c("sunlit" = "gold2", "dark" = "deepskyblue2")

# Standard theme for ordination plots
ord_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 22) +
  theme(
    plot.caption     = element_text(hjust = 0.5, colour = "gray50", size = 7),
    legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 8),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()

# Unified guide formatting for ocean-based plots
ocean_guides <- guides(
  colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3), ncol = 2),

# ---- Analysis-wide configuration parameters ---------------------------------
envfit_p_cutoff <- 0.05                # p-value cutoff for envfit
specialist_threshold_default <- 0.70   # Default niche specialist threshold

# ---- Coastal vs open-ocean affinity settings (section 4) --------------------
# "filtered": marine samples with ocean layer AND size fraction Pico/Nano/Micro (as in the other sections)
# "relaxed" : all marine samples with ocean + coordinates; missing/other size fraction and
#             missing layer are kept and coded as their own level ("unknown")

coastal_indval_alpha   <- 0.05                        # adjusted p-value for coastal/open indicator ASVs (tree panel, section 8)

    run_varpart = TRUE,

    run_permdisp = TRUE,

    run_phylo_driver_specialization = TRUE,

)

# Mapping from lineage names to tree file paths
tree_paths <- list(
  DEEPOL1 = "/Users/ninpo556/Mirror/PhD/Archaeplastids/PacBio_orphans/DEEPOL1/tree/final/DEEPOL1_blast_tree_EukBank.nw",
  DEEPOL2 = "/Users/ninpo556/Mirror/PhD/Archaeplastids/PacBio_orphans/DEEPOL2/tree/blast20261006/DEEPOL2_blast_EukBank.nw",
  DEEPOL3 = "/Users/ninpo556/Mirror/PhD/Archaeplastids/PacBio_orphans/DEEPOL3/tree/cladeC_tree.nw"

# ---- Core helper functions ----
# -- Count detections by categorical variable (for barplots)
count_detections <- function(meta, target_var, target_lineage) {
  meta %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[target_var]])) %>%
    group_by(category = as.character(.data[[target_var]])) %>%
    summarise(
      n_present = sum(.data[[target_lineage]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      lineage = target_lineage,
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# -- Print "section" headers in logs
msg_header <- function(txt) cat("\n", strrep("=", 80), "\n", txt, "\n", strrep("=", 80), "\n", sep = "")

# -- Convert vector safely to numeric, with NA fallback
safe_num <- function(x) {
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.null(x) || all(is.na(x))) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(x[1])
}

# -- Extract one PERMANOVA result term as a tibble
extract_permanova_term <- function(adonis_obj, term) {
  df <- as.data.frame(adonis_obj)
  if (!term %in% rownames(df)) {
    return(tibble(term = term, R2 = NA_real_, F = NA_real_, p = NA_real_))
  }
  tibble(
    term = term,
    R2   = safe_num(df[term, "R2"]),
    F    = safe_num(df[term, "F"]),
    p    = safe_num(df[term, "Pr(>F)"])
  )
}

# -- Summarize categorical trait data (for trait report tables)
make_trait_summary <- function(trait_data, lineage, threshold) {
  pol <- trait_data %>% count(Polarity_class, name = "n_asv") %>%
    mutate(lineage = lineage, domain = "Polarity") %>%
    rename(class = Polarity_class)
  lay <- trait_data %>% count(Layer_class, name = "n_asv") %>%
    mutate(lineage = lineage, domain = "Layer") %>%
    rename(class = Layer_class)
  coast <- if ("Coast_class" %in% names(trait_data)) {
    trait_data %>% count(Coast_class, name = "n_asv") %>%
      mutate(lineage = lineage, domain = "Coastal") %>%
      rename(class = Coast_class)
  } else NULL
  bind_rows(pol, lay, coast) %>%
    group_by(lineage, domain) %>%
    mutate(prop_asv = n_asv / sum(n_asv), threshold = threshold) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# -- Prepare matrix and meta for a lineage (used in ordination/analysis)
prepare_lineage_data <- function(focal_lineage, meta_pa) {
  msg_header(paste("Preparing data for", focal_lineage))
  meta_f <- meta_pa %>%
    filter(.data[[focal_lineage]] == 1) %>%
    filter(habitat == "Marine") %>%
    filter(!is.na(ocean) & ocean != "") %>%
    filter(!is.na(ocean_layer)) %>%
    filter(size_fraction %in% c("Pico", "Nano", "Micro"))
  cat(sprintf("Samples after metadata filtering: %d\n", nrow(meta_f)))
  cat("\n=== Size fraction breakdown ===\n")
  print(meta_f %>% count(size_fraction))
  cat("\n=== Ocean breakdown ===\n")
  print(meta_f %>% count(ocean, sort = TRUE))
  abundance_file <- here("data", "edited", focal_lineage, paste0(focal_lineage, "_filtered_abundance.csv"))
  cat(sprintf("\nLoading abundance data: %s\n", abundance_file))
  abundance <- read.csv(abundance_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
    filter(nreads > 0)
  cat(sprintf("Detected samples: %d\n", n_distinct(abundance$sample)))
  cat(sprintf("ASVs:             %d\n", n_distinct(abundance$amplicon)))
  mat <- abundance %>%
    distinct(sample, amplicon) %>%
    mutate(present = 1L) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = amplicon, values_from = present, values_fill = 0L) %>%
    column_to_rownames("sample") %>%
    as.matrix()
  mat <- mat[, colSums(mat) > 1, drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("Matrix before sync: %d samples x %d ASVs\n", nrow(mat), ncol(mat)))
  samples_keep <- meta_f$sample
  orphans <- setdiff(rownames(mat), samples_keep)
  missing <- setdiff(samples_keep, rownames(mat))
  if (length(orphans) > 0) warning(sprintf("%d samples in matrix not in metadata — removing", length(orphans)))
  if (length(missing) > 0) warning(sprintf("%d samples in metadata not in matrix", length(missing)))
  mat <- mat[rownames(mat) %in% samples_keep, , drop = FALSE]
  mat <- mat[, colSums(mat) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  cat(sprintf("Matrix after sync:  %d samples x %d ASVs\n", nrow(mat), ncol(mat)))
  if (nrow(mat) < 5 || ncol(mat) < 2) {
    stop(sprintf("Too few samples (%d) or ASVs (%d) for ordination.", nrow(mat), ncol(mat)))
  }
  list(meta_f = meta_f, mat = mat)
}

# -- Summarize results for final report row per lineage
build_lineage_report_row <- function(lineage, cfg, dbrda_res, perm_res, n_samples, n_asvs) {
  add_polar <- extract_permanova_term(perm_res$permanova_add, "polar_group")
  add_layer <- extract_permanova_term(perm_res$permanova_add, "ocean_layer")
  int_term <- if (!is.null(perm_res$permanova_int)) {
    extract_permanova_term(perm_res$permanova_int, "polar_group:ocean_layer")
  } else {
    tibble(term = "polar_group:ocean_layer", R2 = NA_real_, F = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
  }
  dbrda_p_overall <- safe_num(dbrda_res$anova_overall$`Pr(>F)`[1])
  env_only_p      <- safe_num(dbrda_res$anova_envonly$`Pr(>F)`[1])
  geo_only_p      <- safe_num(dbrda_res$anova_geoonly$`Pr(>F)`[1])
  env_only_adjR2 <- NA_real_
  geo_only_adjR2 <- NA_real_
  shared_adjR2   <- NA_real_
  resid_adjR2    <- NA_real_
  if (!is.null(dbrda_res$vp)) {
    vp_df <- as.data.frame(dbrda_res$vp$part$indfract)
    # varpart order of individual fractions: [a] X1 alone, [b] shared, [c] X2 alone, [d] residuals
    vp_df$Group <- c("Environment_only", "Shared", "Geography_only", "Residual")
    env_only_adjR2 <- safe_num(vp_df$Adj.R.squared[vp_df$Group == "Environment_only"])
    geo_only_adjR2 <- safe_num(vp_df$Adj.R.squared[vp_df$Group == "Geography_only"])
    shared_adjR2   <- safe_num(vp_df$Adj.R.squared[vp_df$Group == "Shared"])
    resid_adjR2    <- safe_num(vp_df$Adj.R.squared[vp_df$Group == "Residual"])
  }
  permdisp_layer_p <- if (!is.null(perm_res$permtest_layer)) safe_num(perm_res$permtest_layer$tab[1, "Pr(>F)"]) else NA_real_
  permdisp_polar_p <- if (!is.null(perm_res$permtest_polar)) safe_num(perm_res$permtest_polar$tab[1, "Pr(>F)"]) else NA_real_
  tibble(
    lineage = lineage,
    n_samples = n_samples,
    n_asvs = n_asvs,
    permanova_add_polar_R2 = add_polar$R2,
    permanova_add_polar_F  = add_polar$F,
    permanova_add_polar_p  = add_polar$p,
    permanova_add_layer_R2 = add_layer$R2,
    permanova_add_layer_F  = add_layer$F,
    permanova_add_layer_p  = add_layer$p,
    permanova_int_R2 = int_term$R2,
    permanova_int_F  = int_term$F,
    permanova_int_p  = int_term$p,
    permdisp_layer_p = permdisp_layer_p,
    permdisp_polar_p = permdisp_polar_p,
    dbrda_overall_p = dbrda_p_overall,
    env_only_p      = env_only_p,
    geo_only_p      = geo_only_p,
    varpart_env_only_adjR2 = env_only_adjR2,
    varpart_geo_only_adjR2 = geo_only_adjR2,
    varpart_shared_adjR2   = shared_adjR2,
    varpart_residual_adjR2 = resid_adjR2,
    ran_permdisp_interaction = isTRUE(cfg$run_permdisp_interaction)
  )
}

# ---- Record session info for full reproducibility ----
cat("Notebook session started on: ", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n")
sessionInfo()
```

## 1. Data Loading

```{r data-load}
# ==============================================================================
#                  DEEPOL Biogeography - Data Loading Chunk
# ==============================================================================

# ---- 1. Sample metadata ------------------------------------------------------
metadata_file <- here("data", "edited", "meta_with_presence_absence.csv")
message("[Data] Loading sample metadata:\n    ", metadata_file)
metadata_all <- read.csv(
  metadata_file,
  header = TRUE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
cat("[OK] Loaded metadata: ", nrow(metadata_all), " rows\n")
# `polar_group` and `sequencing_depth` are created in the data preparation script
# (polar = Arctic Ocean polygon or latitude south of POLAR_SOUTH_CUTOFF); rerun it if this fails
stopifnot(all(c("polar_group", "sequencing_depth") %in% names(metadata_all)))

# ---- 2. World map polygons ---------------------------------------------------
world_map <- map_data("world")
cat("[OK] Loaded world map polygons: ", dplyr::n_distinct(world_map$region), " regions\n")

# ---- 3. Per-lineage abundance tables -----------------------------------------
abundance_tables <- lapply(lineages, function(lin) {
  file <- here("data", "edited", lin, paste0(lin, "_filtered_abundance.csv"))
  message("[Data] Loading abundance table for ", lin, ":\n    ", file)
  if (!file.exists(file)) stop("Abundance data not found: ", file)
  dat <- read.csv(file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("[OK] %s: %d entries, %d unique samples\n", lin, nrow(dat), dplyr::n_distinct(dat$sample)))
  return(dat)
})
names(abundance_tables) <- lineages

cat("[DONE] All data loaded! Abundance tables available as 'abundance_tables[[lineage]]'.\n")
```

## 2. Unfiltered Visualizations

### 2.1 Abundance Maps

```{r abundance-maps, fig.width=11, fig.height=5, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
#                 DEEPOL Biogeography - Global Abundance Maps (shared size scale)
# ==============================================================================

# -- Helper: Select relevant metadata columns for mapping --
sample_coords <- metadata_all %>%
  select(sample, longitude, latitude) %>%
  mutate(longitude = as.numeric(longitude),
         latitude = as.numeric(latitude)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(longitude) & !is.na(latitude))

# 1. Gather all nonzero abundances for fixed scale across all lineages
all_abundances <- unlist(lapply(abundance_tables, function(tab) tab$rel_abundance_pct))
nonzero_abundances <- all_abundances[all_abundances > 0 & !is.na(all_abundances)]
global_min <- min(nonzero_abundances)
global_max <- max(nonzero_abundances)

message(sprintf("[INFO] Global relative abundance range: %.4f%% – %.4f%%", global_min, global_max))

legend_breaks <- c(0.005, 0.05, 0.5, 5)
legend_labels <- c("0.005%", "0.05%", "0.5%", "5%")

# 2. Map plotting function
create_abundance_map <- function(lineage, meta, abund, world_map, lineage_colours, outdir, scale_min, scale_max, legend_breaks, legend_labels) {
  this_abund <- abund %>%
    filter(!is.na(sample)) %>%
    group_by(sample) %>%
    summarise(rel_abundance_pct = sum(rel_abundance_pct, na.rm=TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  plot_df <- sample_coords %>%
    left_join(this_abund, by = "sample") %>%
    mutate(marker = if_else(is.na(rel_abundance_pct), "absent", "present"))

  plot_df$rel_abundance_pct <- pmax(0, as.numeric(plot_df$rel_abundance_pct))

  legend_title <- "Rel. abundance (%)"

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(
      data = world_map,
      aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
      colour  = "gray70",
      fill    = "gray90",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data  = plot_df %>% filter(marker == "absent"),
      aes(x = longitude, y = latitude),
      shape  = 4,
      size   = 1,
      colour = "gray60",
      alpha  = 0.4
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data  = plot_df %>% filter(marker == "present"),
      aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, size = rel_abundance_pct, colour = rel_abundance_pct),
      alpha   = 0.75
    ) +
    scale_size_continuous(
      name   = legend_title,
      range  = c(2, 12),
      limits = c(scale_min, scale_max),
      breaks = legend_breaks,
      labels = legend_labels
    ) +
    scale_colour_viridis_c(
      name   = legend_title,
      option = "viridis",
      limits = c(scale_min, scale_max),
      breaks = legend_breaks,
      labels = legend_labels
    ) +
    guides(
      size   = guide_legend(title = legend_title),
      colour = guide_legend(title = legend_title)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-90,90),  breaks = seq(-90,90,by=30)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-180,180), breaks = seq(-180,180,by=60)) +
    coord_quickmap() +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      x = NULL, y = NULL
    )

  print(p)
  out_path <- file.path(outdir, paste0(lineage, "_global_abundance_map.pdf"))
  ggsave(out_path, plot=p, dpi=300, width=11, height=6, bg="white", device="pdf")
  message("[Map saved] ", out_path)
}

for (lin in lineages) {
  create_abundance_map(
    lineage = lin,
    meta = metadata_all,
    abund = abundance_tables[[lin]],
    world_map = world_map,
    lineage_colours = lineage_colours,
    outdir = output_dirs[[lin]],
    scale_min = global_min,
    scale_max = global_max,
    legend_breaks = legend_breaks,
    legend_labels = legend_labels
  )
}
```

### 2.2 Abundance summary statistics

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# DEEPOL Biogeography - Lineage abundance summary statistics (per-sample first)
# ==============================================================================

abundance_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(lineages, function(lin) {
  tab <- abundance_tables[[lin]]

  # 1) collapse to one value per sample (sum of all entries for that lineage/sample)
  per_sample <- tab %>%
    filter(!is.na(sample), !is.na(rel_abundance_pct)) %>%
    group_by(sample) %>%
    summarise(rel_abundance_pct = sum(rel_abundance_pct, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  vals <- per_sample$rel_abundance_pct

  tibble(
    lineage = lin,
    n_samples_with_values       = length(vals),
    mean_rel_abundance_pct      = mean(vals),
    median_rel_abundance_pct    = median(vals),
    sd_rel_abundance_pct        = sd(vals),
    min_rel_abundance_pct       = min(vals),
    max_rel_abundance_pct       = max(vals)
  )
})

# Show in notebook

message("[Summary saved] ", summary_outfile)
```

### 2.3 Occurrence by Habitat / Size Fraction

```{r occurrence-barplots, fig.width=9, fig.height=5, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
#         DEEPOL Biogeography - Occurrence Barplots (Habitat & Size Fraction)
# ==============================================================================
#
# For each lineage, plot:
#   - Samples where lineage was detected in each habitat (bar overlay: total vs. present)
#   - Occurrences across size fractions (count of detections per category)
# Outputs are saved as PDFs in each lineage's output directory.
# ==============================================================================

# Helper: Plot and save barplot of detections by a categorical variable
plot_occurrence_bar <- function(meta, lineage, target_var, lineage_colours, outdir) {
  # Occurrence stats by category
  occ_stats <- meta %>%
    filter(!is.na(.data[[target_var]])) %>%
    group_by(category = as.character(.data[[target_var]])) %>%
    summarise(
      total_samples = n(),
      n_present = sum(.data[[lineage]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      pct = (n_present / total_samples) * 100,
      category = factor(category, levels = category[order(-total_samples)])
    )

  # Plot: total as grey, present as colored overlay
  p <- ggplot(occ_stats, aes(x = category)) +
    geom_col(aes(y = total_samples), fill = "grey90", colour = "grey80") +
    geom_col(aes(y = n_present), fill = lineage_colours[lineage]) +
    geom_text(
      aes(y = n_present, label = ifelse(n_present > 0, paste0(n_present, " (", round(pct, 1), "%)"), "")),
      vjust = -0.5, size = 5, fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    labs(
      x = NULL, y = "Number of samples"
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 22) +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 18),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
    )

  print(p)

  # Save
  out_file <- file.path(outdir, paste0(lineage, "_", target_var, "_occurrence.pdf"))
  ggsave(out_file, plot = p, width = 8, height = 5, bg = "white")
  message("[OK] Saved: ", out_file)
}

for (lin in lineages) {
  # By habitat
  plot_occurrence_bar(metadata_all, lin, "habitat", lineage_colours, output_dirs[[lin]])
  # By size fraction
  plot_occurrence_bar(metadata_all, lin, "size_fraction", lineage_colours, output_dirs[[lin]])
}
```

## 3. Filtering for Downstream Analysis

```{r general-filtering, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
```

## 4. Coastal vs Open-Ocean Affinity

```{r coastal-prep, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
#        DEEPOL Biogeography - Coastal Affinity: Distance to Coast & Background
# ==============================================================================
#
# Prepares the data shared by all coastal vs open-ocean analyses:
#   - Computes the distance to the nearest coastline for every sample
#     (sf + Natural Earth coastline), the coastal/open class and log10 distance.
#   - Builds the marine background: ALL marine samples with usable metadata,
#     whether or not a lineage was detected (needed for detection models).
#   - Adds log10 sequencing depth (`sequencing_depth`) as a covariate.
# Settings (`coastal_filter_mode`, `coast_threshold_km`, ...) are in the setup chunk.
# `polar_group` and `sequencing_depth` come from the data preparation script.
# ==============================================================================

msg_header("COASTAL AFFINITY - STEP 0: DISTANCE TO COAST & BACKGROUND")

coastal_out_dir <- file.path(output_root, paste0("coastal_", coastal_filter_mode))
if (!dir.exists(coastal_out_dir)) dir.create(coastal_out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# ---- 0. Distance to coast ----------------------------------------------------
add_coast_distance <- function(meta) {
  meta <- meta %>% mutate(longitude = as.numeric(longitude),
                          latitude  = as.numeric(latitude))
  coords <- meta %>%
    filter(!is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude)) %>%
    distinct(longitude, latitude)
  pts   <- st_as_sf(coords, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)
  coast <- ne_coastline(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
  idx   <- st_nearest_feature(pts, coast)
  coords$dist_coast_km <- as.numeric(st_distance(pts, coast[idx, ], by_element = TRUE)) / 1000
  left_join(meta, coords, by = c("longitude", "latitude"))
}

stopifnot(all(c("polar_group", "sequencing_depth") %in% names(metadata_all)))

meta_all2 <- add_coast_distance(metadata_all) %>%
  mutate(
    coast_class = ifelse(dist_coast_km <= coast_threshold_km, "coastal", "open"),
    log10_dist  = log10(dist_coast_km + 1)   # +1 km avoids log(0); OR is per 10-fold increase
  )

# ---- Marine background -------------------------------------------------------
# Background: all marine samples with usable metadata (same filters as prepare_lineage_data,
# but WITHOUT requiring the lineage to be present)
coast_bg <- meta_all2 %>%
  filter(habitat == "Marine", !is.na(ocean), ocean != "", !is.na(dist_coast_km))

if (coastal_filter_mode == "filtered") {
  coast_bg <- coast_bg %>% filter(!is.na(ocean_layer), size_fraction %in% coastal_size_fractions)
} else {
  coast_bg <- coast_bg %>% mutate(
    ocean_layer   = ifelse(is.na(ocean_layer) | ocean_layer == "", "unknown", ocean_layer),
    size_fraction = ifelse(is.na(size_fraction) | size_fraction == "", "unknown", size_fraction)
  )
}
cat("\nFilter mode:", coastal_filter_mode, "\n")
cat("Size fractions in background:\n"); print(table(coast_bg$size_fraction, useNA = "ifany"))
cat("Ocean layers in background:\n");   print(table(coast_bg$ocean_layer, useNA = "ifany"))

# Sequencing depth covariate: total reads per sample = column 'sequencing_depth' in the metadata
# (created in data_preparation; `nreads` in the abundance tables is lineage reads per ASV)
coast_bg <- coast_bg %>% mutate(log10_reads = ifelse(!is.na(sequencing_depth) & as.numeric(sequencing_depth) > 0,
                                         log10(as.numeric(sequencing_depth)), NA_real_))
n_no_depth <- sum(is.na(coast_bg$log10_reads))
cat("\nSamples without a usable sequencing depth (dropped from all analyses):", n_no_depth, "\n")
coast_bg <- coast_bg %>% filter(!is.na(log10_reads))
cat("Background after depth filter:", nrow(coast_bg), "samples\n")
cat("Sequencing depth, reads per sample:\n"); print(summary(10^coast_bg$log10_reads))

cat("Marine background samples: ", nrow(coast_bg),
    " | coastal: ", sum(coast_bg$coast_class == "coastal"),
    " | open: ", sum(coast_bg$coast_class == "open"), "\n", sep = "")

# -- Keep only model terms that vary in the data (constant covariates would break lm/glm)
keep_terms <- function(d, terms) {
  terms[vapply(terms, function(t) t %in% names(d) && n_distinct(d[[t]]) > 1, logical(1))]
}
```

```{r coastal-regression, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
#      DEEPOL Biogeography - Coastal Affinity: Detection & Abundance Models
# ==============================================================================
#
# For each lineage:
#   1. Detection (present/absent) ~ log10 distance to coast, logistic regression
#      on all marine samples (odds ratio per 10-fold increase in distance), and
#      the same model with the coastal/open class.
#   2. log10 relative abundance ~ log10 distance to coast, linear model on
#      lineage-positive samples (slope per 10-fold increase in distance).
# Covariates (kept only if they vary): polar group, ocean layer, size fraction,
# log10 sequencing depth. Results are saved as CSVs in the coastal output folder.
# ==============================================================================

msg_header("COASTAL AFFINITY - STEPS 1-2: DETECTION & ABUNDANCE MODELS")

# ---- 1. Detection ~ distance to coast (logistic regression) -------------------
fit_detection <- function(lin, dist_term = "log10_dist") {
  d <- coast_bg %>% mutate(present = as.integer(.data[[lin]] %in% 1))
  rhs <- c(dist_term, keep_terms(d, c("polar_group", "ocean_layer", "size_fraction", "log10_reads")))
  m <- tryCatch(glm(reformulate(rhs, response = "present"), data = d, family = binomial),
                error = function(e) { message(lin, ": glm failed - ", e$message); NULL })
  if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
  tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(lineage = lin, model = dist_term, n = nrow(d), n_present = sum(d$present))
}

res_detect <- bind_rows(
  map_dfr(lineages, fit_detection, dist_term = "log10_dist"),
  map_dfr(lineages, fit_detection, dist_term = "coast_class")
)
write.csv(res_detect, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "coastal_detection_logistic.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n== Detection ~ distance to coast (odds ratios) ==\n")
print(res_detect %>% filter(grepl("log10_dist|coast_class", term)) %>%
        select(lineage, model, term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value, n, n_present))
# log10_dist OR < 1  -> detection more likely closer to the coast (coastal)
# coast_class "open" OR < 1 -> less likely in open ocean than in coastal samples

# ---- 2. Relative abundance ~ distance (lineage-positive samples) -------------
per_sample_abund <- function(lin) {
  abundance_tables[[lin]] %>%
    filter(!is.na(sample), !is.na(rel_abundance_pct)) %>%
    group_by(sample) %>%
    summarise(rel_abund = sum(rel_abundance_pct), .groups = "drop")
}

fit_abund <- function(lin) {
  d <- coast_bg %>% inner_join(per_sample_abund(lin), by = "sample") %>% filter(rel_abund > 0)
  rhs <- c("log10_dist", keep_terms(d, c("polar_group", "ocean_layer", "size_fraction", "log10_reads")))
  m <- tryCatch(lm(reformulate(rhs, response = "log10(rel_abund)"), data = d),
                error = function(e) { message(lin, ": lm failed - ", e$message); NULL })
  if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
  tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE) %>% mutate(lineage = lin, n = nrow(d))
}

res_abund <- map_dfr(lineages, fit_abund)
write.csv(res_abund, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "coastal_abundance_lm.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n== log10(rel. abundance) ~ log10(distance to coast), positive samples ==\n")
print(res_abund %>% filter(term == "log10_dist") %>%
        select(lineage, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value, n))
```

```{r coastal-composition, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
#      DEEPOL Biogeography - Coastal Affinity: ASV Composition & Indicators
# ==============================================================================
#
# Within lineage-positive samples:
#   - PERMANOVA (adonis2, marginal terms) on Jaccard distances of ASV presence/
#     absence, with the coastal class or log10 distance as predictor after the
#     other covariates, plus a matching PERMDISP (betadisper) on the same grouping.
#   - Indicator ASV analysis (multipatt, IndVal.g) for coastal vs open samples,
#     Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted. Requires the 'indicspecies' package.
# These are the slowest steps (999 permutations each).
# ==============================================================================

msg_header("COASTAL AFFINITY - STEPS 4-5: ASV COMPOSITION & INDICATORS")

# -- Sample x ASV presence/absence matrix + aligned metadata for one lineage
# ---- 4/5. ASV-level analyses (presence/absence matrices) ----------------------
build_pa <- function(lin, data = coast_bg) {
  meta_f <- data %>% filter(.data[[lin]] %in% 1)
  mat <- abundance_tables[[lin]] %>%
    filter(nreads > 0) %>%
    distinct(sample, amplicon) %>%
    mutate(present = 1L) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = amplicon, values_from = present, values_fill = 0L) %>%
    column_to_rownames("sample") %>%
    as.matrix()
  mat <- mat[, colSums(mat) > 1, drop = FALSE]                    
  mat <- mat[rownames(mat) %in% meta_f$sample, , drop = FALSE]
  mat <- mat[, colSums(mat) > 0, drop = FALSE]
  mat <- mat[rowSums(mat) > 0, , drop = FALSE]                   
  list(mat = mat, meta = meta_f[match(rownames(mat), meta_f$sample), ])
}

# 4. PERMANOVA (marginal terms) + PERMDISP on coastal class
coast_permanova <- function(lin, predictor = c("coast_class", "log10_dist"), data = coast_bg, tag = "all") {
  predictor <- match.arg(predictor)
  b <- build_pa(lin, data)
  meta <- b$meta
  if (nrow(meta) < 8) { message(lin, ": too few samples for PERMANOVA."); return(NULL) }
  dist_mat <- vegdist(b$mat, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
  rhs <- c(keep_terms(meta, c("polar_group", "ocean_layer", "size_fraction", "log10_reads")), predictor)
  set.seed(42)
  ad <- adonis2(reformulate(rhs, response = "dist_mat"), data = meta,
                permutations = 999, by = "margin")
  grp <- if (predictor == "coast_class") factor(meta$coast_class) else
    cut(meta$log10_dist, breaks = quantile(meta$log10_dist, 0:4 / 4, na.rm = TRUE),
        include.lowest = TRUE)
  pd <- if (nlevels(droplevels(grp)) > 1 && min(table(droplevels(grp))) >= 2) {
    permutest(betadisper(dist_mat, droplevels(grp)), permutations = 999)$tab[1, "Pr(>F)"]
  } else NA_real_
  as.data.frame(ad) %>%
    rownames_to_column("term") %>%
    mutate(lineage = lin, stratum = tag, predictor = predictor,
           n_samples = nrow(meta), permdisp_p = pd)
}
res_perm <- bind_rows(
  map_dfr(lineages, coast_permanova, predictor = "coast_class"),
  map_dfr(lineages, coast_permanova, predictor = "log10_dist")
)
write.csv(res_perm, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "coastal_permanova.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n== PERMANOVA (marginal) + matching PERMDISP ==\n")
print(res_perm %>% filter(term %in% c("coast_class", "log10_dist")) %>%
        select(lineage, predictor, n_samples, R2, `F`, `Pr(>F)`, permdisp_p))

# 5. Indicator values (coastal vs open)
run_indval <- function(lin, data = coast_bg, tag = "all") {
  if (!requireNamespace("indicspecies", quietly = TRUE)) {
    message("Install 'indicspecies' to run indicator analysis."); return(NULL)
  }
  b   <- build_pa(lin, data)
  if (ncol(b$mat) < 2 || nrow(b$mat) < 6) {   # multipatt needs a matrix with >= 2 ASVs
    message(lin, " (", tag, "): fewer than 2 ASVs shared by >1 sample, skipping indicator analysis.")
    return(NULL)
  }
  grp <- factor(b$meta$coast_class)
  if (nlevels(grp) < 2 || min(table(grp)) < 3) {
    message(lin, ": too few samples in one coastal class for indicator analysis."); return(NULL)
  }
  set.seed(42)
  mp <- tryCatch(
    indicspecies::multipatt(b$mat, grp, func = "IndVal.g",
                            control = permute::how(nperm = 999)),
    error = function(e) {
      message(lin, " (", tag, "): multipatt failed (", conditionMessage(e), "); matrix is ",
              nrow(b$mat), " samples x ", ncol(b$mat), " ASVs, groups: ",
              paste(names(table(grp)), table(grp), collapse = ", "))
      NULL
    })
  if (is.null(mp)) return(NULL)
  as_tibble(mp$sign, rownames = "ASV") %>%
    mutate(lineage = lin, stratum = tag, p_adj = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"))
}
res_indval <- map_dfr(lineages, run_indval)
if (nrow(res_indval) > 0) {
  write.csv(res_indval, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "coastal_indicator_asvs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\n== Indicator ASVs (adjusted p < 0.05) ==\n")
  print(res_indval %>% filter(p_adj < 0.05))
}

# ---- Per-ASV coastal/open class for the phylogenetic trees (used in section 8) ----
# Based on the indicator analysis on all samples (stratum "all"); `label` matches the tree tips.
# ASVs not in the matrix (e.g. present in a single sample) are "Not tested" in the tree.
coastal_asv_class <- if (nrow(res_indval) > 0) {
  res_indval %>%
    filter(stratum == "all") %>%
    mutate(Coast_class = case_when(
      p_adj < coastal_indval_alpha & s.coastal == 1 ~ "Coastal indicator",
      p_adj < coastal_indval_alpha & s.open == 1    ~ "Open indicator",
      TRUE                                          ~ "Not significant"
    )) %>%
    select(lineage, label = ASV, Coast_class, indval_stat = stat, indval_p_adj = p_adj)
} else {
  tibble(lineage = character(), label = character(), Coast_class = character(),
         indval_stat = numeric(), indval_p_adj = numeric())
}
write.csv(coastal_asv_class, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "coastal_asv_class_for_trees.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nCoastal/open class per lineage (ASVs):\n")
print(coastal_asv_class %>% count(lineage, Coast_class))
```

```{r coastal-confounds, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
#       DEEPOL Biogeography - Coastal Affinity: Confound & Robustness Checks
# ==============================================================================
#
# Are "coastal vs open" patterns really about distance to coast, or about ocean
# layer, polar region, size fraction or study that travel with it?
#   6a. Association (Cramer's V) of coastal class with the other variables.
#   6b. Study structure and leave-one-study-out odds ratios.
#   6c. Distance effect within strata (sunlit, dark, non-polar, polar), and a formal
#       test whether the distance effect differs between layers / polar regions.
#   6d. Indicator ASVs within strata.
# ==============================================================================

msg_header("COASTAL AFFINITY - STEP 6: CONFOUND & ROBUSTNESS CHECKS")

cramers_v <- function(x, y) {
  tab <- table(x, y)
  if (min(dim(tab)) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  ch <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE))
  as.numeric(sqrt(ch$statistic / (sum(tab) * (min(dim(tab)) - 1))))
}
confound_vars <- keep_terms(coast_bg, c("ocean_layer", "polar_group", "size_fraction"))

# 6a. How strongly is coastal class tied to the other variables?
#     (Cramer's V: ~0.1 weak, ~0.3 moderate, >0.5 strong)
confound_assoc <- map_dfr(c("background", lineages), function(set) {
  d <- if (set == "background") coast_bg else coast_bg %>% filter(.data[[set]] %in% 1)
  map_dfr(confound_vars, function(v) {
    tibble(sample_set = set, variable = v, n = nrow(d),
           cramers_v = cramers_v(d$coast_class, d[[v]]),
           chisq_p   = suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table(d$coast_class, d[[v]])))$p.value)
  })
})
write.csv(confound_assoc, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "confound_coast_vs_covariates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n== 6a. Association of coastal class with other variables ==\n"); print(confound_assoc)
cat("\nCoastal class x ocean layer (background, % within layer):\n")
print(round(100 * prop.table(table(coast_bg$ocean_layer, coast_bg$coast_class), 1), 1))
cat("\nCoastal class x polar group (background, % within group):\n")
print(round(100 * prop.table(table(coast_bg$polar_group, coast_bg$coast_class), 1), 1))

# 6b. Study / project structure (column name differs between metadata versions)
study_col <- intersect(c("study", "study_id", "project", "bioproject", "dataset", "cruise"), names(coast_bg))[1]
if (!is.na(study_col)) {
  cat("\n== 6b. Study column used: ", study_col, " ==\n", sep = "")
  coast_bg$study_tmp <- coast_bg[[study_col]]
  print(coast_bg %>% group_by(coast_class) %>%
          summarise(n_samples = n(), n_studies = n_distinct(study_tmp),
                    top_study_share = max(table(study_tmp)) / n(), .groups = "drop"))
  # Leave-one-study-out: range of the distance odds ratio when each large study is dropped
  big <- names(which(table(coast_bg$study_tmp) >= 20))
  loso <- map_dfr(lineages, function(lin) {
    map_dfr(big, function(s) {
      d <- coast_bg %>% filter(study_tmp != s) %>% mutate(present = as.integer(.data[[lin]] %in% 1))
      rhs <- c("log10_dist", keep_terms(d, c("polar_group", "ocean_layer", "size_fraction", "log10_reads")))
      m <- tryCatch(glm(reformulate(rhs, "present"), data = d, family = binomial), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
      tibble(lineage = lin, dropped_study = s, OR = exp(coef(m)["log10_dist"]),
             p = summary(m)$coefficients["log10_dist", 4])
    })
  })
  write.csv(loso, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "confound_leave_one_study_out.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nLeave-one-study-out odds ratio for log10 distance (range per lineage):\n")
  print(loso %>% group_by(lineage) %>%
          summarise(OR_min = min(OR), OR_max = max(OR), n_sig = sum(p < 0.05), n_runs = n(), .groups = "drop"))
} else {
  message("No study/project column found in metadata: set study_col by hand to run 6b.")
}

# 6c. Do the detection / abundance results hold within strata?
strata <- list(
  `sunlit only`    = coast_bg %>% filter(tolower(ocean_layer) == "sunlit"),
  `dark only`      = coast_bg %>% filter(tolower(ocean_layer) == "dark"),
  `non-polar only` = coast_bg %>% filter(polar_group == "non-polar"),
  `polar only`     = coast_bg %>% filter(polar_group == "polar")
)
detect_in <- function(d, lin, label) {
  d <- d %>% mutate(present = as.integer(.data[[lin]] %in% 1))
  if (sum(d$present) < 20) return(NULL)
  rhs <- c("log10_dist", keep_terms(d, c("polar_group", "ocean_layer", "size_fraction", "log10_reads")))
  m <- tryCatch(glm(reformulate(rhs, "present"), data = d, family = binomial), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
  tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE) %>% filter(term == "log10_dist") %>%
    transmute(lineage = lin, stratum = label, response = "detection", estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value,
              n = nrow(d), n_present = sum(d$present))
}
abund_in <- function(d, lin, label) {
  d <- d %>% inner_join(per_sample_abund(lin), by = "sample") %>% filter(rel_abund > 0)
  if (nrow(d) < 20) return(NULL)
  rhs <- c("log10_dist", keep_terms(d, c("polar_group", "ocean_layer", "size_fraction", "log10_reads")))
  m <- tryCatch(lm(reformulate(rhs, "log10(rel_abund)"), data = d), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(m)) return(NULL)
  tidy(m, conf.int = TRUE) %>% filter(term == "log10_dist") %>%
    transmute(lineage = lin, stratum = label, response = "abundance (slope)", estimate, conf.low, conf.high,
              p.value, n = nrow(d), n_present = nrow(d))
}
res_strata <- imap_dfr(strata, function(d, label) {
  bind_rows(map_dfr(lineages, ~ detect_in(d, .x, label)),
            map_dfr(lineages, ~ abund_in(d, .x, label)))
})
write.csv(res_strata, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "confound_stratified_models.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n== 6c. Distance effect within strata ==\n"); print(res_strata)

# 6d. Do indicator ASVs survive within strata, and are they really layer/polar ASVs?
res_indval_strata <- bind_rows(
  imap_dfr(strata, function(d, label) map_dfr(lineages, ~ run_indval(.x, data = d, tag = label)))
)
ind_calls <- bind_rows(res_indval, res_indval_strata) %>%
  mutate(class = case_when(s.coastal == 1 ~ "coastal", s.open == 1 ~ "open", TRUE ~ "none")) %>%
  filter(p_adj < 0.05) %>%
  select(lineage, ASV, stratum, class, stat, p_adj)
write.csv(ind_calls, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "confound_indicator_asvs_by_stratum.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# 6c(ii). Formal test: does the distance effect DIFFER between layers / polar regions?
test_interaction <- function(lin, modifier = c("ocean_layer", "polar_group"),
                             response = c("detection", "abundance")) {
  modifier <- match.arg(modifier); response <- match.arg(response)
  d <- coast_bg
  if (modifier == "ocean_layer") {                       # sunlit vs dark only (drop "unknown")
    d <- d %>% mutate(ocean_layer = tolower(ocean_layer)) %>% filter(ocean_layer %in% c("sunlit", "dark"))
  }
  if (response == "detection") {
    d <- d %>% mutate(y = as.integer(.data[[lin]] %in% 1))
    if (sum(d$y) < 20) return(NULL)
  } else {
    d <- d %>% inner_join(per_sample_abund(lin), by = "sample") %>% filter(rel_abund > 0) %>%
      mutate(y = log10(rel_abund))
    if (nrow(d) < 20 || n_distinct(d[[modifier]]) < 2) return(NULL)
  }
  others <- setdiff(keep_terms(d, c("polar_group", "ocean_layer", "size_fraction", "log10_reads")), modifier)
  rhs0 <- c("log10_dist", modifier, others)
  rhs1 <- c(rhs0, paste0("log10_dist:", modifier))
  fit <- function(rhs) {
    if (response == "detection") glm(reformulate(rhs, "y"), data = d, family = binomial)
    else lm(reformulate(rhs, "y"), data = d)
  }
  m0 <- tryCatch(fit(rhs0), error = function(e) NULL)
  m1 <- tryCatch(fit(rhs1), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(m0) || is.null(m1)) return(NULL)
  a <- if (response == "detection") anova(m0, m1, test = "Chisq") else anova(m0, m1)
  tibble(lineage = lin, modifier = modifier, response = response, n = nrow(d),
         interaction_p = a[2, ncol(a)])
}
res_inter <- bind_rows(lapply(lineages, function(lin)
  bind_rows(lapply(c("ocean_layer", "polar_group"), function(mod)
    bind_rows(test_interaction(lin, mod, "detection"), test_interaction(lin, mod, "abundance")))))) %>%
  mutate(p_adj_BH = p.adjust(interaction_p, method = "BH"))
write.csv(res_inter, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "confound_distance_interactions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\n== 6c(ii). Interaction tests: distance x layer / polar group ==\n")
print(res_inter, n = Inf)
```

```{r coastal-forest, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
# ==============================================================================
#       DEEPOL Biogeography - Coastal Affinity: Forest Plot (detection & abundance)
# ==============================================================================
#
# Effect of a 10-fold increase in distance to the coast, overall and within strata:
#   - Detection: odds ratio (< 1 = more likely closer to the coast, > 1 = offshore)
#   - Abundance: fold change in relative abundance in positive samples (10^slope)
# Uses res_detect, res_abund (coastal-regression chunk) and res_strata (confound chunk).
# Strata with < 20 positives were not modelled and are absent from the plot.
# ==============================================================================

msg_header("COASTAL AFFINITY - FOREST PLOT")

overall <- bind_rows(
  res_detect %>%
    filter(model == "log10_dist", term == "log10_dist") %>%
    transmute(lineage, stratum = "all samples", response = "Detection (odds ratio)",
              effect = estimate, low = conf.low, high = conf.high, p = p.value),
  res_abund %>%
    filter(term == "log10_dist") %>%
    transmute(lineage, stratum = "all samples", response = "Abundance (fold change)",
              effect = 10^estimate, low = 10^conf.low, high = 10^conf.high, p = p.value)
)

strat <- res_strata %>%
  mutate(
    response = ifelse(response == "detection", "Detection (odds ratio)", "Abundance (fold change)"),
    is_abund = response == "Abundance (fold change)",
    effect = ifelse(is_abund, 10^estimate, estimate),
    low    = ifelse(is_abund, 10^conf.low, conf.low),
    high   = ifelse(is_abund, 10^conf.high, conf.high)
  ) %>%
  transmute(lineage, stratum, response, effect, low, high, p = p.value)

forest_df <- bind_rows(overall, strat) %>%
  mutate(
    stratum  = factor(stratum, levels = rev(c("all samples", "sunlit only", "dark only",
                                              "non-polar only", "polar only"))),
    response = factor(response, levels = c("Detection (odds ratio)", "Abundance (fold change)")),
    sig      = p < 0.05
  )
write.csv(forest_df, file.path(coastal_out_dir, "coastal_forest_plot_data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

p_forest <- ggplot(forest_df, aes(x = effect, y = stratum, colour = lineage)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = low, xmax = high), height = 0.25, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = sig), size = 2.6, fill = "white") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = lineage_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 16, `FALSE` = 21),
                     labels = c(`TRUE` = "p < 0.05", `FALSE` = "p ≥ 0.05"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_grid(lineage ~ response, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Effect of a 10-fold increase in distance to the coast (log scale)\n< 1: higher closer to the coast  |  > 1: higher offshore",
       y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.background = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

print(p_forest)
ggsave(file.path(coastal_out_dir, "coastal_forest_plot.pdf"), p_forest, width = 8, height = 7, bg = "white")
```
